result.title: Microcontroller Architecture
bullets: A microcontroller is an integrated circuit that combines a CPU, RAM, program memory, input/output ports, timers, and communication peripherals into a single chip.
The CPU is the central processing unit that executes instructions and controls the flow of data within the microcontroller.
RAM (Random Access Memory) is used for temporary data storage during program execution, allowing the microcontroller to hold variables and intermediate results.
Program memory (often flash memory) stores the firmware or software instructions that the microcontroller executes.
Input/output (I/O) ports allow the microcontroller to interact with external devices such as sensors, actuators, and other peripherals.
Timers are hardware modules that measure time intervals and can be used for tasks like generating precise delays, controlling PWM signals, or synchronizing events with external signals.
result.summary: Microcontrollers are designed to be compact, cost-effective solutions for embedded systems. They integrate essential components like a CPU, memory, and I/O interfaces into a single chip, enabling them to control hardware and interact with the external world efficiently. This architecture makes microcontrollers ideal for applications ranging from simple consumer electronics to complex industrial systems.

result.title: Examples of Microcontrollers
bullets: Arduino Uno: Popular open-source board widely used for beginner projects and prototyping.
ESP32: Feature-rich microcontroller with built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth capabilities.
STM32: Powerful 32-bit microcontroller family based on ARM Cortex-M processors.
PIC: Microchip technology series known for industrial and embedded control applications.
AVR: Atmel 8-bit RISC architecture powering many traditional microcontroller boards.
result.summary: Key microcontroller platforms commonly used in embedded systems range from beginner prototyping boards like Arduino to connected chips like ESP32 and industrial hardware like STM32, PIC, and AVR.
